definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese wooden sandals with an elevated base supported by two wooden blocks. Worn with traditional clothing like yukata and kimono.

examples.japanese: {浴衣|ゆかた}に{下駄|げた}を{履|は}いて{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I went out wearing a yukata and geta.

examples.japanese: {下駄|げた}の{音|おと}がカラコロと{響|ひび}く。
examples.english: The sound of geta clogs echoes 'kara-koro'.
examples.notes: カラコロ is onomatopoeia for geta sounds

examples.japanese: {夏祭|なつまつ}りでは{下駄|げた}を{履|は}く{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people wear geta at summer festivals.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころ、{祖母|そぼ}の{家|いえ}で{下駄|げた}を{履|は}いて{遊|あそ}んだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I wore geta and played at my grandmother's house.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{下駄|げた}を{履|は}く{機会|きかい}が{少|すく}なくなったが、{花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい}のときだけは{浴衣|ゆかた}に{下駄|げた}で{出|で}かける。
examples.english: These days there are fewer opportunities to wear geta, but I go out in a yukata and geta just for fireworks festivals.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Geta are traditional Japanese footwear, now mainly worn with summer yukata at festivals. The distinctive clacking sound they make when walking is culturally evocative.

TYPES:
・{駒|こま}{下駄|げた} (standard two-toothed geta)
・{一本|いっぽん}{歯|ば}{下駄|げた} (single-toothed geta, worn by tengu)

EXPRESSIONS:
・{下駄|げた}を{預|あず}ける (to entrust a decision to someone - lit. 'entrust one's geta')
・{下駄|げた}を{履|は}かせる (to add extra points/pad numbers - lit. 'put geta on')
